theme: 3 terms on placing views on the screen: the view that lines up subviews for you, the screen area clear of the notch and home indicator, and the padding inside a view's edges

terms.definition: A view that lines up its subviews in a row or a column and creates their layout rules for you.
terms.example: Put the three buttons in a Stack View, then you only need constraints for the stack.
terms.code:
let row = UIStackView(
    arrangedSubviews: [icon, title])
row.axis = .horizontal
row.spacing = 8

terms.definition: The part of the screen not covered by the notch, the home indicator or system bars, where content is safe to show.
terms.example: Pin the toolbar to the Safe Area, or it hides under the home indicator.

terms.definition: The padding inside a view's edges that other views can line up against.
terms.example: Use the Layout Margins, so every card has the same inner padding.
terms.code:
card.directionalLayoutMargins = .init(
    top: 12, leading: 16,
    bottom: 12, trailing: 16)
let g = card.layoutMarginsGuide
label.leadingAnchor.constraint(
    equalTo: g.leadingAnchor).isActive = true

quizzes.question: What do you call the padding inside a view's edges that other views can line up against?
Which view lines up its subviews in a row or a column for you?

video.description:
Learn to explain where views sit on the screen in UIKit: Stack View, Safe Area & Layout Margins, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Stack View - A view that lines up its subviews in a row or a column and creates their layout rules for you.
Safe Area - The part of the screen not covered by the notch, the home indicator or system bars, where content is safe to show.
Layout Margins - The padding inside a view's edges that other views can line up against.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Stack View, Safe Area & Layout Margins in UIKit by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
스택 뷰, 세이프 에어리어, 레이아웃 마진 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Stack View - A view that lines up its subviews in a row or a column and creates their layout rules for you.
한국어: 스택 뷰: 하위 뷰를 가로나 세로 한 줄로 늘어놓고 레이아웃 규칙을 대신 만들어 주는 뷰

Safe Area - The part of the screen not covered by the notch, the home indicator or system bars, where content is safe to show.

한국어: 레이아웃 마진: 다른 뷰가 맞춰 정렬할 수 있는, 뷰의 가장자리 안쪽 여백

landscape.hook: The buy button hides under the home indicator. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Why is the button hiding?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, on newer iPhones the `buyButton` sits under the home indicator.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You pinned the Stack View to the bottom of `view`, not the Safe Area.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Safe Area skips the notch and the home indicator. Pin to its bottom anchor instead.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. And now the button touches the screen edges.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Stack View fills the whole width. Give it Layout Margins.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, spacing only adds gaps between `price` and `buyButton`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So Layout Margins are the padding inside the edges?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, and turn on `isLayoutMarginsRelativeArrangement` so the Stack View uses them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Safe Area for the bottom, Layout Margins for the padding.
Three buttons in a row? A Stack View does the layout for you.
